objective.value: Determine the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant gas-jet diffusion flames under different co-flow conditions in microgravity; quantify the sooting propensity of different fuels and the effects of burner diameter and co-flow velocity on luminous flame length and smoke point.

sources.note: PSI-107 objective: identify laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames, quantify sooting propensity of different fuels, and validate luminous flame shape vs residence time

PSI-107 researchArea 'Combustion Science', subResearchArea 'Fire Safety'; objective and hypothesis study the fundamental smoke-point/sooting behaviour of laminar flames
SPICE document frames the work as continuing 'fundamental phenomena' on stability and extinction of jet diffusion flames

relevance_notes.value: Fundamental soot/smoke-point study named in the challenge brief's hardware section (SPICE flow duct in the MSG). Soot controls the radiative heat emitted from microgravity flames, so smoke-point and luminous-flame-length data feed models of heat release and fire spread that support spacecraft fire safety and material selection.

sources.note: Challenge brief, 'Hardware': SPICE used the SPICE flow duct in the MSG
SPICE document: soot dominates heat emitted from flames and control of that heat is critical for preventing fire spread on Earth and in space

value: The smoke-point metric is a classical tool in Earth fire modelling and for understanding soot growth and emission by flames
Better prediction of heat release and soot behaviour in non-buoyant practical flames such as jet-engine and furnace combustors
Possible insights for fuel formulation and combustion processes

sources.note: PSI-107 researchImpacts: refine computational models, improve understanding of soot generation, and possible insights to better fuel formulations and combustion processes
SPICE document 'Earth Applications': smoke point is used in fire modelling and to predict heat release from non-buoyant flames in practical combustors
